newsitem.title: JAPAN: EPA minister says not concerned now about weak yen.
newsitem.headline: EPA minister says not concerned now about weak yen.

text.p: Economic Planning Agency Minister Taro Aso told reporters on Tuesday that he is not concerned about the impact of the weaker yen against the dollar on the Japanese economy for now.
Aso said wild fluctuations in foreign exchange rates are not welcomed by companies as exchange rates sometimes determine whether the companies can turn a profit.
"Stable currencies are desirable for the Japanese economy," he said.
Asked if the government will ask monetary authorities to stop the weakening of the yen, Aso said he has no such plans now.
"I'm not concerned now about any impact of the weak yen on the economy," he said.
